findings.title: Resumed round re-enters with no prior-round outputs, breaking 910 feedback and the 305 gate
findings.description:
D3 sets the prior-round context to empty on re-entry and defers rehydration to "911/305 territory." Neither consumer supports that:
- Slice plan entry 8 (910 Part A) has dispatch read the prior round's REVIEW findings from `prior_outputs`. A resumed round N ≥ 2 would run the un-fed prompt, so the #42 symptom returns on every resume past round 1.
- 305's Screen 0 treats "no prior review result in `prior_outputs`" as round 1 and returns `PASS` with `no_prior_round: true`. A resumed round ≥ 2 therefore passes the addressed leg without checking anything, which is the fail-open this slice exists to remove.
- 305 lists resume rehydration as an unverified Phase 6 item (Decision 5, Risk Assessment). Its success criteria contain no resume test, so the hand-off points at work no slice owns.

The data is available: the doc says the prior results live in the paused run's `action_results`, which `_append_step` persists. Before implementation, the design must choose one of two options. Either rehydrate the prior round's review and action results from state on re-entry, with a test that a resumed round ≥ 2 receives the findings and the gate sees the prior review. Or refuse re-entry at iteration ≥ 2 with an explicit error until rehydration exists. The sentence saying this is "stated in the round contract (Part C docs)" should also be fixed, because Part C in scope covers only the WARNING.

findings.title: Part B adds a resume capability without a scope classification
findings.description: The 900 architecture excludes "new features or capabilities." The doc says there is "no existing notion of 'resume into step X at iteration N'" (lines 89-96), so Part B adds one. Slice plan entry 10 moved 305 out of 900 on exactly this ground. The parts cannot be split to shrink scope: Part A without Part B makes resume re-run the loop from round 1, which D1 forbids. The doc should state in Technical Scope why Part B is part of the bug fix (restoring the `max:`/`until:` contract on resume). It should also reconcile the "Changing checkpoint semantics — unchanged" exclusion (lines 137-138) with D1, which changes what a `Continue` resolution does inside a loop.

findings.title: Pause-time WARNING fires on the designed path
findings.description: Under D1, a pause followed by resume is the intended path. The loop continues at the paused round and nothing is abandoned. Part C nonetheless logs a WARNING "rounds not run" on every in-loop pause. That is a false alarm on the happy path and labels suspension as abandonment. D4's justification ("stays correct even if a future D1 makes abandonment intentional") gets this backwards: the WARNING is wrong under the current D1. Under D1, abandonment happens only when the human chooses `Exit` or the run ends while paused. Move the WARNING to that point, or make the pause-time message INFO. Verification step 4 (lines 357-359) and the Part C test list must follow.

findings.title: Silent clamp and DEBUG-only ignore break the observability rules
findings.description: `start_from_iteration` is "clamped to `>= 1`" when the target is a loop. That is a silent fallback, which CLAUDE.md forbids. The non-loop case is logged at DEBUG. A non-loop target carrying a non-zero iteration means the state and the pipeline disagree, which is a WARNING-level event under the failure-mode rule in `review-code.md`, and it needs a test asserting that signal. Replace the clamp with an explicit error or a WARNING, and raise the ignored case to WARNING.

findings.title: Re-entry edge cases are unspecified
findings.description:
The design does not say what happens in two cases:
- **Recorded iteration absent or 0 for a paused loop.** The clamp turns this into a silent restart at round 1. That resets the count and grants extra rounds, against D1.
- **Pipeline edited between pause and resume so `max` is below the recorded iteration.** `range(start, max + 1)` is empty. The doc does not say whether zero rounds takes the `on_exhaust:` branch, passes the loop, or errors. A pass is the trust defect this slice is meant to remove.

Each case needs an explicit outcome, a log level, and a test.

findings.title: FAILED steps become resumable: outside the plan entry, and it widens `each:`/`fan_out:` restarts
findings.description: Slice plan entry 13 scopes the fix to checkpoint pauses inside loops. Adding `FAILED` changes resume for every pipeline, as the Risk Assessment acknowledges. The justification (same mechanism) is true, but the doc does not treat the change as a requirement. Its consequence is also unhandled. A failed `each:`/`fan_out:` step will now re-run all branches on resume, including branches that already succeeded, which duplicates model spend and side effects. The Known Limitation (lines 365-377) covers only a checkpoint inside an `each:` body and calls Part A "a strict improvement" without accounting for this. Either move `FAILED` to a follow-up with its own plan entry, or add the plan change and specify the `each:`/`fan_out:` handling for failed steps, with a test.

findings.title: Overweight for a maintenance slice; cut the restated sections
findings.description:
The 900 architecture asks for "lighter-weight" maintenance slices, and the plan rates this one 2/5. The doc runs to about 400 lines. Cut:
- Verification Walkthrough steps 2–5 (lines 324–363) restate the Success Criteria. Keep step 1, the reproduce-before-fix step.
- Known Limitation (lines 365–377) restates the Excluded bullet (lines 130–136). Keep one.
- Component Structure (lines 282–292) repeats Technical Scope and D2–D4.
- "Which loops are affected" (lines 103–112) repeats plan entry 13.

Keep the two verified facts, D1's rationale, the rejected alternatives, and the risk section.

findings.title: Integration points missing from frontmatter and the consumer list
findings.description: `interfaces: []` is empty. This slice changes the `execute_pipeline` signature that the CLI calls, and it changes the resumed-round contract that 910 (findings feedback), 911 (per-iteration commits and `revision_number:` stamping on re-run rounds), and 305 (prior-round lookup) all read. 911 records `interfaces: [305]` for a comparable dependency, so the convention exists. Record these consumers and tie the round contract to the first finding.
